messages:
sara_dev: Proposal: add an "onramp" phase to our spot-backed inference autoscaler. Motivation: when we scale from warm standby to full capacity we see request amplification + NIC/kernel spikes that blow out tail latency for ~1m. TL;DR: stagger pod readiness, limit initial concurrency, and use network-aware placement per AZ.

kevin_infra: +1 on thinking about network. Do you have metrics? what windows are we talking about?

sara_dev: we see 95th jump from ~120ms -> ~450ms for ~60s after scaleout in eu-west-1; kube-proxy conntrack and NIC TX queueing are the main bottlenecks. Also cold model shard loads hit NVLink and cause kernel latency. sample graph: https://graphs.internal/redwood/spot-scaleout/eu-west-1

raj_sre: idea: add a 'ramp' annotation to PodSpec so the scheduler spreads startups over Xs. Also envoy should start in warm mode (no new upstream connections) for N seconds.

lina_ml: can we limit batch sizes for newly created replicas for first N tokens? that would reduce kernel/spike amplification on model side.

kevin_infra: quick config sketch for discussion:

```yaml
autoscaler:
  target: gpu-inference-group
  scale_out_trigger: queue_length > 50
  onramp:
    window_seconds: 45         # spread readiness over this window
    max_concurrent_new_replicas: 6
    initial_batch_limit: 8     # cap batch size for new pods
    network_smoothing: true    # enable AZ-aware placement + conntrack pacing
  cooldown_seconds: 300
  surge_headroom: 0.12        # keep reserved capacity for interrupts
  fallback_model_variant: quantized-dense
```

sara_dev: exact numbers will be tuned via canary. also enforce: do not create >2 new replicas in same AZ within onramp window, to avoid single-AZ NIC saturation.

autoscale-bot: [ALERT] scaleout started for gpu-inference-group in eu-west-1 — 24 -> 40 replicas at 2024-06-01T12:34:56Z

deploy-bot: logs show conntrack_high events at 2024-06-01T12:35:05Z: "nf_conntrack: table full" — adding conntrack tuning to runbook (sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max).

raj_sre: runbook suggestion: sysctl tweaks, kube-proxy conntrack max bump, ephemeral port range expansion, and probe/grace delay (so new pods are Ready=false for 10s). Also add alert if conntrack drops > 10/s.

sara_dev: decision: canary the onramp in eu-west-1 for 2 hours with traffic shaping. Metrics to watch: p95 latency, p99 GPU utilization, conntrack drops, model cold-load times, and cost impact. @kevin_infra can you create the canary? :thumbsup:

kevin_infra: yep I'll create canary config and a PR. Rolling at 14:00 UTC. I'll include per-AZ placement constraints and a grace probe delay. cc @lina_ml for batch capping.

lina_ml: I'll prepare a small model-side change that caps batch size for replicas with replica_age_seconds < 120 and emit replica_age_seconds metric. Should reduce kernel spikes.

raj_sre: add an alert rule: if p95_latency increases > 25% during canary, auto-rollback on the autoscaler change. Also monitor pod startup error rate.

sara_dev: I'll update the doc + runbook with config snippets and rollback steps. Link: https://go.redwood/sops/onramp-proposal

kevin_infra: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/1234 — contains autoscaler onramp support + AZ spread policy. Please review.

sara_dev: thanks everyone — will monitor dashboards and post updates. :eyes:
